summary: Theorem3.1 is false for a permitted two-deletion/two-insertion stream; Theorem3.2's proof uses an invalid absolute-error PAC-Bayes step and unjustified context concentration. The theoretical superiority comparison fails; empirical improvements are not refuted.
limitations: No author-code execution or empirical reproduction.
P2 establishes a proof failure, not a numerical FLAIR checkpoint counterexample.
Static source inspection partial; benchmark provenance, all plots and external citations not verified.

independent_verification.source_and_assumptions: Directly read p6 Theorem3.1, p19 E.1 and Algorithm2. The theorem allows mixed insertions/deletions, any frozen trained model, and iid final records from any continuous distribution. No restriction excludes an exact initial count model with i=j=2.
independent_verification.decisive_reasoning: Delete both old Uniform(0,1) records and insert two fresh independent Uniform(0,1) records: k=4, s=r=2, final sample iid continuous and changed almost surely. Every old and final interval count is in {0,1,2}; the absolute difference is <=2 for every query and realization, whereas the claimed lower bound is3. Expectation and supremum order cannot overcome a pathwise cap.
independent_verification.alternative_and_dependency: The proof explicitly infers median +/-1 from possible extreme support, which is invalid; moreover +/-k cannot be reached when exactly two insertions and two deletions occur. No adversarial-operation restriction is stated. The p6 mandatory retraining/theoretical superiority comparison directly uses this lower bound.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained for false core lower bound; empirical adaptation can still work. No general corrected bound asserted.

problems.claim: Context error uniformly O(1/sqrt(rho)) with only bounded parameter KL and iid final records.
problems.check: KL0 with constant unit loss disproves the absolute-risk implication; needed range, iid context, empirical error, uniform event absent.
problems.result: Invalid core derivation; theorem under extra hypotheses unresolved.
problems.counterevidence: Triangle decomposition and Gaussian-tail integration algebra valid; diagnostic is not a trained-FLAIR counterexample.

independent_verification.source_and_assumptions: Read p20 E.2 together with p6 theorem and p19 FIFO Algorithm2. KL is over model parameters, error is absolute cardinality prediction discrepancy, and iid current records do not imply iid changing query-result memory.
independent_verification.decisive_reasoning: The displayed PAC-Bayes quantity lacks an empirical/approximation risk term. Identical prior/posterior and unit loss make KL0 but do not make risk vanish; at rho1000 delta.05 the asserted term is0.0387. The diagnostic targets the invoked implication, not a FLAIR checkpoint. Hoeffding also requires independent bounded quantities and an established equality between query prediction error and sample-average error; those are not supplied. Pointwise to supremum additionally needs uniformity.
independent_verification.alternative_and_dependency: Triangle inequality and Gaussian-tail integration are valid; adequate training is not mathematically equated to an approximation-risk condition. Interpreting the first term as a generalization gap changes the claim and requires retaining empirical risk.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained for invalid derivation supporting the central drift-immunity/superiority guarantee; truth under additional assumptions unresolved. Repair needs explicit loss range, empirical/approximation error, sampling/drift and uniformity conditions; no claim all experiments fail.
